baer-heitev/1:ב: (ב) "And there is none" — meaning there is no obligation but there is a custom; Levush wrote that the custom is to give Purim money for each and every member of the household, even for children, and pregnant women also give for the unborn child per the Gemara; and it is stated in a mishnah: every minor whose father began to weigh coins on his behalf does not cease. In a place where the custom is to give the money as half-shekel to the chazan there is no prohibition in the matter, for whoever gives gives with intent for the custom — Mishna Berurah siman 694. But they do not fulfill matanot laevyonim through this unless they divide some of it for the poor — Magen Avraham. Shelah wrote that half-shekel and certainly matanot laevyonim and mishloach manot do not come from maaser money, and if one wishes to add he adds from non-maaser — Maharil in responsum siman 56; see Kanfei Nesharim and Yad Aharon. Money one planned in his heart to distribute on Purim day he may not change — Beit Yosef in name of Hagahot Asheiri; see Beit Yosef siman 258.
beur-hagra/3:_: s.k. 63 they are not meticulous etc. Likewise per Rif's text and so in Yerushalmi there.
biur-halacha/1:ד: (ד) One should give three half-groats in these countries — behold the common way is to interpret "half-groats" as half of three groats, namely what we call in our country (half-groats), and it does not seem so in Darkei Moshe — see there; perhaps it is another coin name called thus in the country he wrote about, where he wrote that a half-groat is nine small pashutim. In our country now we do not have this coin. Per our country it appears a medina issues a small coin called half-groat, but it is not an important coin at all even if one gives three halves unless he also gives for his small children. I saw some collectors who first put three half-reichstaler in the charity bowl, and when one comes to give the half-shekel the collector gives him in place of his money the three half-reichstaler and he puts them in the bowl — but this is not clear, for if the collector gives them only as a loan for a few moments and the giver does not intend to acquire them for charity, behold this is not giving at all and he only deceives himself. If the collector's intent is truly to acquire for him and he gives them to charity, this is advice only for the first one and not for those after, since they already became charity the collector has no permission to exchange them for three half-groats; perhaps since they already practiced thus it is as if all givers to charity stipulated explicitly that the collector may do so. Behold in the time of the Gra a Polish half-zahuv was found and it is written in Maaseh Rav that he would give only one Polish half-gold, but now this coin is not found at all unless one gives half-groats or half-reichstaler. One whom the Holy One blessed be He helps that he can give one reichstaler in memory of half-shekel and three half-groats for what is written in the parashah three times terumah — so wrote the latter Rama: fortunate and good for him.
eliyah-rabbah/4:_: [4] [Levush] forbidden etc. and they cross rivers for the sake of the meal etc. and Sefer HaMinhag and Sefer Imrei Kal.
eshel-avraham/1:_: to two poor people. A city dweller who sent portions to a country dweller and they reached him on the 14th — he fulfilled if he knew he would not eat them except on the 15th, for we follow the joy of the recipient — likewise in Yad Aharon siman 694 who wrote that one who sent portions abroad and they arrived there on Purim he fulfilled even at the time he sent from his house the time had not yet arrived — the same law here; see Darkei Moshe what he wrote in name of Mahari Weil and Maharil and Shaarei Chaim siman 693. The same if he sent portions and the sender was prevented — he did not fulfill, for everything depends on the joy of the recipient — so concluded in responsum Masat Moshe, unlike what Bnei Chayei wrote — see there.
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] Every person is obligated to give etc., even a poor person supported from charity, as with four cups of Pesach — unlike other charity where he is obligated only once a year to fulfill the mitzvah of charity as written in Yoreh Deah siman 248 and 249. Bach. Avodah Zarah s.k. 1. Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Turei Zahav letter 1 — see there letter 1 letter 1 and Peri Chadash wrote that a poor person supported from charity is exempt from matanot laevyonim, but Mateh Yehudah wrote the main law is as Bach and his colleagues and similar to mishloach manot as Peri Chadash himself wrote below siman 695 that a poor person supported from charity is obligated — see there. So agreed Birkei Yosef letter 2 and in his book Machber letter 1 Shulchan Gavoah letter 2 Nehar Shalom letter 1 Chayei Adam letter 2 Bigdei Yesha. Chayei Adam general rule 165 letter 28. Mishna Berurah letter 1:
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (4) there. Every person is obligated to give etc., and what we do not bless on mishloach manot and matanot laevyonim as we bless on reading the Megillah — Rashba wrote in responsum siman 18 because perhaps they will not receive and more see there the reason for all mitzvot we do not bless on them — see there. Nevertheless one may say leshem yichud before giving with this text: leshem yichud Kudsha Berich Hu etc., behold I come to fulfill the mitzvah of matanot laevyonim instituted by Mordechai and Esther to give on this day two gifts to two poor people to repair the root of this mitzvah in the supernal place. And may it be pleasant etc., and so he says before mishloach manot and before the day's meal:
levushei-serad/1:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 5 from Rama's language. It is difficult — on the contrary it seems from Rama specifically the collectors, and from the Mechaber he should have proved; but the poor etc. he omitted city dwellers — it appears since he omitted there is not so much proof; but Rama who emended the beginning of Mordechai's words and did not emend also their end — he should have emended "but the poor and city dwellers" etc. — we learn that in this he does not hold like Mordechai, and it requires study.
machatzit-hashekel/3:א: (s.k. 3) From age twenty — this is per Raavad etc. in tractate Shekalim chapter 1 mishnah 3, and Tiferet Yisrael wrote Raavad's reason: two verses are written in parashat Ki Tisa — in one it is written "this they shall give, all who pass among the counted, half a shekel"; and the second verse is written "all who pass among the counted from twenty years and above shall give the terumah"; and Chazal expounded there were two types of half-shekel, one from which the sockets for the Mishkan were made and one from which communal offerings were taken all year, and that which was for offerings applied also for generations; and Raavad holds the second verse "from twenty years" refers to half-shekel for offerings, therefore we require specifically age twenty. But Rambam holds the first verse that writes plainly "all who pass among the counted" etc. refers to offerings, and if so since he is thirteen years old when he is called gadol he is obligated in half-shekel for offerings; and if so since the half-shekel we give on Purim is remembrance of those half-shekalim given for offerings, and they established on Purim as we learn in mishnah on 1 Adar they announce about shekalim that each bring his half-shekel — therefore our custom depends on the dispute of Raavad and Rambam above. And it is in mishnah every minor etc. in that mishnah — and Rambam specifically: his father is obligated but if the father died the minor is exempt, for the father cannot obligate his minor son. Tiferet Yisrael wrote to explain Raavad's words that he wrote also a minor after his father's death is obligated — it refers where the father left property to the minor and then the obligation falls on the father's property — see there.
machatzit-hashekel/3:ב: In a place etc. but they do not fulfill etc. even the chazan is poor — nevertheless since he is included in the chazan's hire he pays his debt with matanot laevyonim.
magen-avraham/1:א: (א) Two gifts — from his own and not from maaser money [Shelah], and if he wishes to add he adds from non-maaser [Maharil in responsum siman 56], and it is written in Maor that he should not give them before Purim lest they eat them before Purim.
magen-avraham/2:א: (א) One may not change — Beit Yosef wrote in name of Hagahot Asheiri: money one planned in his heart to distribute on Purim day he may not change it — end of his words; see Beit Yosef siman 258 and Choshen Mishpat siman 212 Shaarei Chaim.
magen-avraham/2:ב: (ב) And specifically the collectors, but etc. In Tur it implies even city dwellers may not change, and so from Rama's words here; but Mordechai wrote explicitly city dwellers may change, and if so their law is like other charity as written in Yoreh Deah siman 256 s.k. 4.
mishnah-berurah/2:א: (א) (6) One may not change Purim money — meaning money the collectors gathered to distribute to the poor for the Purim meal; he cannot change them to say enough with less and the remainder falls to the charity fund, but they buy calves in quantity with all the money and what remains that they will not eat on Purim they sell and it falls to the charity fund [gemara]. Beit Yosef wrote in name of Hagahot Asheiri: money one planned in his heart to distribute to the poor on Purim day he may not change it, and the reason is he holds charity has sanctity law and he must fulfill his thought even though he did not express it with his lips.
peri-megadim/1:_: Obligated — Taz and Eliyah Rabbah letter 1, and he added that in mishloach manot too he is obligated and it is simple, and so somewhat in gemara; matanot laevyonim one might have thought is included in charity and exempt — it teaches us. Peri Chadash in 695 wrote he is obligated in mishloach manot and here wrote exempt from matanot laevyonim — requires study; perhaps all were in the miracle category as woman case 695 s.k. 4, and he may give food or money — I did not find now how much is measure of gifts. It appears to me l'chatchila he must give a gift to a poor person something fit to enjoy on Purim, food or money he can spend on Purim; see Tur who ruled the poor may not change the money like R' Meir per baraita of artisans ch. 8 of gemara collection Purim to Purim, and therefore the poskim and Mechaber ruled as them in s.k. 2 except the poor may change but the homeowner must give what he can enjoy on Purim. Though one could say the opposite that Tur ruled in gemara collection Purim to Purim that they gave with intent it be consumed on Purim (Peri Chadash here for R' Meir: reason one who changes without owner's knowledge is a robber, and though we do not hold so on Purim certainly they gave with this intent) — not so when the homeowner gives him a garment and clothes one could say permitted for all; nevertheless it appears l'chatchila he should give something he can enjoy on Purim — requires study; see Yoreh Deah 248 s.k. 1 and Shach 1 and 693 in Shach note 11 and Rosh note 11; the same here a poor person supported from charity gives two gifts to two poor people and they return and give him. I was in doubt regarding gift to poor whether it helps on condition to return, and mishloach manot does not help because mitzvah is food and drink they rejoice on Purim — case 695 portions language of preparation min and Imrei Esh there explained — requires study. And three half-shekel if they distribute to poor people do they fulfill matanot laevyonim — see Magen Avraham 3 and it will be explained there; and what Rama wrote in s.k. 1 three half-groats that half-shekel is upon them — Darkei Moshe wrote half-groat is nine small pashutim and per se ten since ten gerah is half-shekel, and per se meaning including the half-groat itself, and study is needed because coins changed to know the measure.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:א: (א) Two gifts. Avodat HaTumah; see Peri Chadash who holds a poor person is exempt from matanot laevyonim and obligated in mishloach manot, and Birkei Yosef wrote as Bach and Taz as ruled in Yoreh Deah siman 248 that even a poor person supported from charity must give from what was given him; in Machatzit HaShekel he wrote so in Mateh Yehudah; see there in name of Zera Yaakov that if he gives money he must give measure that acquires three eggs' worth of food, and if he gives foods he must give measure of three eggs of bread — so appears per straightforward reading; per this if he distributes to poor people a portion to each of a perutah he does not fulfill, and still needs to be settled — till here his language, and I do not have the book itself to know his reason; in every place of giving a perutah see Pesachim daf 32 and Gittin daf 47 in Tosafos there, and perhaps he learned from what is written in Chullin perek Reishit HaGez that he give him weight of five selaim to make from it a small garment as it says "you shall give him" that there be enough for a gift, and so Rambam wrote in chapter 10 Laws of Bikkurim and Shulchan Aruch Yoreh Deah siman 353 "give him that there be enough for a useful gift"; per this one could say the same here it is not called a gift unless there is enough for a useful gift, namely enough for meal measure; indeed there daf 138 it is stated that what we derive enough to make a small garment from scripture "to stand and serve" is derived, and see responsum Noda B'Yehuda mahadura tinyana Yoreh Deah siman 201 who wrote regarding challah separation there are two mitzvot: one to remove tevel prohibition which has no Torah measure, and second to fulfill giving mitzvah to kohen which has Torah measure as written "you shall give" enough for giving etc., and there he debated Tosafos in Gittin daf 47 and wondered on them — see there at length (see Ramban in Gittin there who wrote for a monetary matter a perutah suffices and get is different — see there); and I wondered he did not mention mishnah perek Reishit HaGez and from Mishneh LaMelekh one could learn matanot laevyonim is the same, and the examiner will see the matters are close — see there; and what is written in name of Leket Yosher one who gives to one measure of two gifts etc. — it appears from gemara language and poskim certainly he does not fulfill with less than two poor people; see Peri Chadash who challenged saying two gifts to each poor person as challenged in Yoma regarding "and he shall place on the two goats" etc. — see there; in Birkei Yosef he extended on this — see there in Eliyah Rabbah in name of Rambam: better to increase matanot laevyonim than to increase his meal and mishloach manot to friends, for there is no great and splendid joy except to rejoice the heart of poor, orphans, widows and converts, similar to the Divine Presence of whom it is said "to revive the lowly spirit and restore the broken heart" — till here his words.
shaarei-teshuvah/1:ב: (ב) And there is no Avodat HaTumah. What is written in a place where they practice giving the money as half-shekel to the chazan etc. — in Machatzit HaShekel he erred through mistake that fell in Magen Avraham and the reference to seif 2 "one may not change Purim money" etc. is missing, and on this Magen Avraham relies as explained in Mishna Berurah and as written in Yad Efrayim; it never entered the mind there would be a custom to give half-shekel to the chazan, and Avodat HaTumah who added on his own the words half-shekel did not aim well and it is a stumbling block causing charity collectors who are the hand of the poor to diminish the power of the poor from this charity given for half-shekel to give to the chazan — thus Mishna Berurah: what is practiced in several communities that they give all Purim money to the shaliach tzibbur who reads the Megillah alone and do not distribute Purim money to the poor at all — is it permitted to do so or must the custom be abolished because we learn collection Purim to Purim? Answer: certainly it is not proper to do so, and the kosher custom is to distribute to the poor; however this is specifically how they collected explicitly for the poor etc. or the city's custom etc.; but in those places that already practiced giving all Purim money to the chazan who reads the Megillah I do not see prohibition, for everyone who gives etc. has intent for the chazan, for there is no law of Purim money here, and though it rolls on people's tongues to call them Purim money, the matter does not depend on the name but on the collection — the matter depends on collection, and so Rashi explained collection Purim: money the collectors gathered from city members to distribute to poor for Purim meal etc. — not so in our case they never collected with intent for the poor etc. — end of his words; it is clear their way in those places was to collect from beit kenesset to give to the chazan who reads Megillah and it was called Purim money, and Mishna Berurah ruled thus; but one must not be lenient regarding half-shekel, and one who says custom per Avodat HaTumah — we do not listen, for it is mistaken custom and if they practiced they must abolish it; to me it appears God-fearing shlichei tzibbur who wished to merit half-shekel because of these words of Avodat HaTumah — I showed them it is error and they retracted and withdrew their hand from it henceforth; and what Magen Avraham brought Avodat HaTumah "but they do not fulfill through this" etc. — this too is clear it refers to that money given to collectors called Purim money.
